chapter: Image, travel and Black, Brown and Beige
title: First visit to New Orleans
summary: Bands and relatives greeted them, Greer was called cousin, and hospitality never stopped.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: And New Orleans, man. First time we went to New Orleans, had a station down there. They brought our baggage car and our Pullman there, that's how we traveled, right in the station. And man, them cats had cars lined up for three blocks, private cars then, bands. Band always -- what the hell was the name of them bands?

I know. They were there, had signs up, "Welcome Home Barney Bigard" Everybody's cousin, you know. Wellman Braud, Braud was there. And we'd heard so much about New Orleans, man. I'm the last one off the train. And don't you know, them cats knew me. Knew me. "Come on." And right away, I said, "I'm from here, too." I ain't never been there before in my life. And right away they call me in Creole, "cousin". I said, "Man."
And from the time we got there until the time we left, it was food, food, food. I never seen so much hospitality in my life. Everybody was inviting us out somewhere,

you know. Right away I fell in with a guy named Benjy. He had a big restuarant. He looked like a white guy. And I couldn't buy nothing at that restuarant, bar, couldn't buy nothing. And food galore. They'd say, "Hey, Sonny, what you like?" I said, "Man, I love hardshell crabs. Blue-clawed things, big ones." He said, "All right, I'm going to give you a present when you go." Actually, I forgot all about it. Man, the night we left, I come down to the station and the porter say, "Hey, Sonny, these guys brought you a present down there from a friend."
